title: LogParser-LLM: Advancing Efficient Log Parsing with Large Language Models

problem.claim: Log parsing converts raw logs into structured formats needed for downstream analysis.

gap.claim: Contemporary system complexity and dynamic logs challenge existing automatic parsing techniques.

contributions.claim: LogParser-LLM integrates LLM capabilities with semantic insights and statistical nuances for log parsing.
The method supports online parsing without hyper-parameter tuning or labeled training data.
The work proposes a metric for parsing granularity and integrates human interaction to calibrate granularity to user needs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe LogParser-LLM as a novel log parser and describe the granularity metric as new.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method was evaluated on the Loghub-2k and LogPub benchmarks.
On LogPub, across 14 datasets averaging 3.6 million logs per dataset, the method used 272.5 LLM invocations on average and achieved 90.6% grouping F1 and 81.1% parsing accuracy.
The authors report higher efficiency and accuracy than pattern-based, neural network-based, and existing LLM-enhanced parsers.

narrative_sequence.summary: Logs support system diagnostics, security analysis, and performance optimization, while parsing structures them for downstream analysis.
Existing automatic parsing techniques face difficulties from contemporary system complexity and dynamic logs.
The work introduces an LLM-integrated parser combining semantic and statistical information, with online parsing and no labeled training data or hyper-parameter tuning.
The work addresses parsing granularity using a new metric and human calibration.
Benchmark evaluations report efficiency, accuracy, and outperformance of prior parser categories.

source_observation.claim: Combining semantic LLM capabilities with statistical information is reported to support adaptive log parsing without labeled training data.

interpretation.claim: Hybrid semantic-statistical designs may reduce dependence on task-specific supervision while retaining structured parsing behavior.

application.claim: This pattern may apply to other dynamic text-to-structure pipelines that need rapid adaptation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond log parsing or under what operating constraints.

source_observation.claim: The method lets users calibrate parsing granularity through human interaction.

interpretation.claim: User-controllable granularity can make structured extraction better aligned with downstream needs.

application.claim: Interactive granularity controls may be useful in analytical systems where different users require different levels of structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not describe the interaction workflow or its user effort and reliability.

unknowns: Details of the parsing algorithm and LLM configuration are omitted.
Benchmark protocols, baselines, statistical variation, and error analysis are omitted.
The proposed metric's definition and validation are omitted.
